sources.title: Humane Intelligence Inc nonprofit tax record EIN 93-1491311

reading.body:
Humane Intelligence is recorded as a 2022 Texas nonprofit with no AI products, no litigation, and no MCP servers, but 126 Texas law exposure entries.

The only substantial data point is the law exposure count. Everything else in the record is an absence: no products, no cases, no MCP servers, no aliases. A nonprofit founded in 2022 and headquartered in Katy, Texas, with a website that returned only a placeholder message at collection time, leaves almost nothing to characterize what the organization actually does.

The 126 Texas law exposure entries are the one figure that carries weight, and the data does not explain what they represent. They could be filings, citations, or registry entries. Without that definition, the count cannot be read as risk, activity, or scale. It is a number attached to a Texas code reference and nothing more.

For AI specifically, this record supports no claim about compute, data centers, or power. There is no product, no infrastructure, and no disclosed operation to connect to the grid. The honest reading is that the data is thin, and the absences should be treated as gaps in collection rather than as facts about the organization.

profile_text.body:
Humane Intelligence is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in 2022 and headquartered in Katy, Texas, United States. According to its website, it is dedicated to breaking down barriers to AI deployment for social good and collaboratively designs and runs evaluations intended to make AI systems more accountable, responsible, and fair.

The organization describes three main service lines. AI red teaming is a semi-structured testing approach to assess and improve the safety and effectiveness of AI models and systems, offered as a paid service using software the organization released under an open source license in September 2026. AI contextual evaluations are described as rigorous, mixed-method, bespoke evaluations of a model or system's performance for a specified problem space, with an ontology-based contextual AI evaluation method developed in 2026 and offered as a paid service. Bias bounties are collaboratively designed challenges bringing together researchers, impacted communities, and domain experts; the final self-hosted bias bounty closed in November 2025, and the first bias bounty on Zindi, described as a global data science challenge platform, launched in August 2026. The organization's web application was built for data collection at hosted red teaming events and for contextual evaluation services, was released as open source in September 2026, and new client-facing software was slated for October 2026.

The record lists no tracked products, no lawsuits, and no MCP servers. It records nonprofit tax registration under EIN 93-1491311 and a Texas law exposure count of 126.
